name: Mangosteen (Garcinia mangostana)
short: Case report: severe lactic acidosis with mangosteen juice taken as a supplement. Pericarp extract by mouth, 11 adults for 24 weeks: minor side effects only. Skin patch: contact allergy in 2 of 30.
text: This entry covers mangosteen taken by mouth (fruit juice, pericarp extract) and applied to the skin; no adverse-event data were found for mangosteen gel placed in gum pockets. No human safety data were found for purified alpha-mangostin; the by-mouth data below are for mangosteen juice and mangosteen extracts (pericarp extracts where the abstract says so). Serious harm (case report, by mouth): a case of severe lactic acidosis (a dangerous build-up of acid in the blood) was associated with mangosteen fruit juice used as a dietary supplement; the abstract gives no further details. In a 24-week study of the polar fraction of mangosteen pericarp extract taken by mouth by 11 healthy Thai volunteers, only minor and tolerable side effects were reported, no serious side effects were documented, and blood tests showed no liver damage or kidney dysfunction. That study tested the extract's polar fraction, and its authors note that the cytotoxic activity of mangosteen extract has been found in the nonpolar fraction. In a 26-week randomised pilot study in 22 obese women with insulin resistance, given behavioural therapy alone or with a mangosteen extract (the abstract does not say which part of the fruit was used or how the extract was taken; 20 completed), no side effect attributable to treatment was reported. In an 8-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of a mangosteen juice blend in obese people with raised C-reactive protein (44 randomised, 40 completed), no side effects were reported in any group, and laboratory and heart-tracing (ECG) checks showed no clinically significant changes. In an 8-week randomised, placebo-controlled trial in 104 people with gingivitis, a propolis and mangosteen extract complex taken by mouth (a combination) caused no significant adverse events. The abstract of a 24-week placebo-controlled trial of mangosteen pericarp extract added to usual treatment in 152 people with bipolar depression gives no adverse-event data. On the skin (a different route): in a closed patch test of a mangosteen pericarp extract hydrogel patch in 30 healthy volunteers, there was no irritation, but two volunteers had a delayed allergic contact dermatitis, and the authors advise against the patch for people who have reacted to mangosteen. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
